editorial.marketOverview: The Nasdaq-100 remains in a cautiously bullish, event-driven reversal attempt. Nvidia formally reinstated Jensen Huang and Reuters reported the Nasdaq-100 up 6.6% intraday and Nvidia over 31%. This confirms a powerful cash-market reaction, not a close or durable trend.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the 09:57 ET assessment, additional Reuters reporting substantiates the already recognized catalyst and puts the Nasdaq-100 intraday gain at 6.6%. No second catalyst or directional change was established. The curated Open Watch feed remains at its 13:57 UTC refresh and does not yet capture the reinstatement.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The breadth of reported AI buying makes a recovery attempt plausible, but violent post-liquidation moves can be dominated by short covering. Missing synchronized semiconductor relative strength, breadth, volatility and curve observations prevent a higher-conviction regime upgrade.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday: unusually strong leadership-driven cash rebound with high fade risk. Tuesday: follow-through test against consumer sentiment and Dell results. Wednesday: inflation, growth and Fed communication may determine whether relief buying becomes durable. The base case remains a fragile bullish rebound, not a confirmed new uptrend.
editorial.bullCase: Leadership continuity restores confidence in the AI supply chain, semiconductors outperform QQQ, breadth broadens, and volatility subsides while yields stabilize. Such follow-through would validate Monday's reversal.
editorial.bearCase: A gap-and-fade, renewed export-control pressure, rising yields or disappointing macro data exposes the rally as short covering. Failed semiconductor participation would make the bullish bias vulnerable.
editorial.watchNext: Check Monday closing QQQ, Nasdaq-100, SOX/SMH and advance-decline breadth, synchronized VXN/VIX and correctly scaled 10Y/2Y yields; verify FedWatch and matched Brent/WTI contracts. Track HPE, Dell, consumer confidence and Wednesday macro releases, distinguishing anticipated effects from observed responses.
